advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Recompute blocking_count from the scope-narrowed verdict findings (or document that scan_blocking_findings is intentionally unscoped) so it agrees with scanner_verdicts.
evidence: security.py:116 `for finding in await _verdict_findings(req, report):` — verdict loop uses scoped findings
security.py:153 `blocking_count=report.blocking_count,` — count still from unscoped report
mediator.py:88 `blocking_count=blocking_count(findings, threshold=self.threshold),` — computed over all findings
draft_pull_request.py:1951 `scan_blocking_findings=scan.blocking_count,` — the unscoped count is propagated to the promotion outcome
advisory.finding: ScanChangeResult.blocking_count is still derived from report.blocking_count (the mediator's count over ALL findings), while scanner_verdicts is now computed over the scope-narrowed findings. The two become inconsistent under the default 'changed' scope: on an established repo, scanner_verdicts can all be 'pass' while blocking_count (surfaced as scan_blocking_findings) is > 0.
scenarios: An established repo with pre-existing HIGH findings in untouched files, PR touches only clean files: scanner_verdicts={semgrep:pass} but scan_blocking_findings reports the pre-existing count.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute blocking_count over the same set returned by _verdict_findings (e.g. blocking_count(verdict_findings, threshold=report.threshold)) rather than reusing report.blocking_count.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether two-dot (base..ref) or three-dot (base...ref) range is intended for PR-scope attribution and align code + doc accordingly.
evidence: scan_scope.py:56 `args = ["git", "diff", "--name-only", f"{base_ref}..{ref}"]`
draft_pull_request.py:1830-1832 `ref=commit_sha` and `base_ref=params.base_sha` — base and head can diverge before the scan runs
docs/gate-engine.md:174 documents `git diff --name-only <base_ref>..<ref>` matching the code, so behavior is intentional but the two-dot semantics differ from typical PR diffs
advisory.finding: The changed-file set uses a two-dot git range (`base_ref..ref`), which diffs the two commit tips directly. For pull-request-style attribution the conventional range is three-dot (`base_ref...ref`), which limits to changes since the merge-base; with two-dot, commits landed on base after branch-off show up as differing files and can wrongly attribute pre-existing findings to the change (or vice versa).
scenarios: Long-lived feature branch where main advanced after branch-off; a file changed only on main appears in the two-dot changed set and a pre-existing finding there becomes attributable/blocking.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a changed_paths test with non-empty base_ref and empty ref asserting a None fallback.
evidence: scan_scope.py:47 `if not base_ref or not ref:`
test_scan_scope.py only calls `changed_paths("/ws", "", "head1")` (empty base_ref); no test passes `ref=""` with a non-empty base_ref
Named violating input: `changed_paths("/ws", "base1", "")` exercises only the `not ref` disjunct
advisory.finding: The empty-`ref` half of the added guard `if not base_ref or not ref:` in changed_paths is untested; only the empty-`base_ref` case is covered by test_an_empty_base_ref_falls_back_to_the_repository_and_blocks.
scenarios: A caller supplies a resolved base_ref but an empty ref; the fallback-to-repository behavior is only assumed, not asserted
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized case to the fallback test invoking `changed_paths("/ws", "base1", "")` and asserting `changed is None` plus the warning.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In is_attributable, treat an unmatched-but-existing path defensively (log and/or normalize both sides) so a genuine finding in a changed file is not silently stripped of blocking power.
evidence: scan_scope.py:102 `if path in changed: return True` — exact string equality against git diff output
scan_scope.py:104-112 only the not-a-file branch logs and keeps blocking power; the file-exists-but-unmatched case falls through to `return False` (line 112) with NO warning
gate_engine.py:46-48 finding location is built from the review engine's `comment.get('path')`: `location = f"{path}:{line}"` — a semi-trusted, unnormalized source
scan_scope.py:74 changed set is raw `out.splitlines()` from `git diff --name-only` with no unquoting/normalization
scan_scope.py:88-90 prefix is only stripped when `head.startswith(f"{root}/")`; otherwise an absolute head is returned unchanged
scan_scope.py:104 `os.path.isfile(os.path.join(repo_root, path))` — os.path.join(root, '/abs') returns '/abs', so the check escapes repo_root
scan_scope.py:112 a matching absolute file returns False (finding does not block)
advisory.finding: is_attributable silently drops a finding from the blocking set (returns False, no warning) when the finding's location path does not string-match any entry in the `git diff --name-only` set BUT the file exists in the checkout. Because the finding path comes from the review engine's `comment.path` (map_review_findings) and the changed set is raw `git diff --name-only` output (which may be C-quoted for special/unicode chars under default core.quotePath, or use a different relative form), a genuine finding in a truly-changed file can lose its power to block with no log signal — a fail-open path that contradicts the module's stated fail-safe design.
merged_from: relative_location_path can return an absolute path (when the checkout prefix does not match), and is_attributable then calls os.path.isfile(os.path.join(repo_root, path)); os.path.join with an absolute second argument discards repo_root and probes the absolute path directly. A finding whose location names an absolute path that exists outside repo_root is treated as attributable=False (dropped from blocking) rather than kept — a defense-in-depth gap in the attribution boundary.
scenarios: A real Critical finding lands in a file the PR genuinely modified, but git emits the path C-quoted or in a form that differs from the engine-reported path; the file exists so isfile passes, `path in changed` is False, and the finding is silently excluded from the verdict — gate passes.
Path separator / relative-root divergence between the diff output and the scanner-reported location causes attributable=False for an in-scope finding.
advisory.suggested_fix: Normalize both the git diff paths and the finding path (unquote git C-quoting, os.path.normpath, POSIX separators) before the `path in changed` comparison, and log a warning when a finding is excluded so silent verdict-dropping is observable.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the new default scan_scope='changed' silently narrowing existing scan_change block verdicts is an intended, documented behavior change with a migration note (SCAN_SCOPE=repository) for audit consumers.
evidence: scripts/config.py:107: `scan_scope: str = "changed"`

services/orchestration/temporal_activities/security.py:116: verdict loop now iterates `await _verdict_findings(req, report)` instead of the prior `for finding in report.findings:` (see diff), so with the default 'changed' scope only attributable findings set a verdict

services/orchestration/temporal_activities/security.py:90-93: `if scope != CHANGED_SCOPE: return list(report.findings)` — repository-wide blocking is only reachable via non-default SCAN_SCOPE=repository
docs/gate-engine.md:174: `repository` restores the earlier behaviour, where any finding anywhere fails the gate` — confirms the default is a behavior change from prior semantics
blocking.finding: The new scan_scope config field defaults to 'changed', which silently changes the existing scan_change gate behavior: previously any finding in report.findings could set a scanner verdict to 'block', now only findings located in git-diff-changed files do so by default. Consumers relying on repository-wide blocking (e.g. scheduled audits invoking the same scan_change activity) will see verdicts flip to 'pass' unless they explicitly set SCAN_SCOPE=repository.
scenarios: An established repository with pre-existing findings that previously blocked promotion now promotes PRs by default because those findings are not in the changed file set
A scheduled/audit invocation of scan_change that relied on repository-wide blocking silently returns 'pass' verdicts until SCAN_SCOPE=repository is set
